assumptions: This is a planning-stage opportunity with no assumed customers, signed partners, or completed legal and technical validation.

The operating model remains strictly non-custodial: a registry-capable counterparty performs all guarantee purchase, holding, transfer, and cancellation actions, while the startup supplies reconciliation and evidence software.
The revised modest SME workspace fee or wholesale partner licence is the relevant pricing model because the original 800-2000 PLN monthly SME subscription is contradicted by bundled incumbent offers.

Buyer-specific invoice allocation and evidence-pack generation are technically feasible if a partner lawfully supplies the necessary registry and consumption data; access, mandate scope, and demand frequency remain unknown.
The founder initially keeps the corporate job, contributes roughly 10-15 hours per week, and limits initial capital to about 50000 PLN.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Ten documented SME or buyer cases where bundled supplier certificates fail a specific site, customer, or reporting-period requirement, together with a registry-capable partner's signed pilot terms confirming lawful data and confirmation access, pricing and revenue share, expected manual exception workload, and measurable CAC, payback, retention, and volume economics.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The proposed control point—the reconciled record linking metered consumption, a named customer, unique certificate attributes, and confirmed cancellation—is coherent and addresses a real evidentiary workflow. However, the research shows that registries and suppliers already perform core issuance, aggregation, and confirmation functions, so the remaining insight is a narrower workflow and claims-control layer rather than a clearly neglected structural gap.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Customers can face recurring requests for auditable renewable-origin evidence, and anti-overstatement rules make accurate documentation useful. Yet no reviewed case shows that existing supplier evidence fails a buyer-specific requirement, while Axpo says renewable-origin coverage is included without extra fees and Energa already provides collective cancellation. Pain for exceptional audit cases is plausible, but willingness to pay for the proposed add-on is unvalidated and ordinary-SME willingness to pay is directly challenged.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A non-custodial software layer can start within available capital and could have high software gross margin at scale. The original price is contradicted, revised pricing is hypothetical, partner share and manual exception cost are unknown, and neither CAC nor payback is underwritten. At the stated 2 PLN per MWh administration yield, more than 1 TWh plus meaningful subscription revenue and durable channel control are needed for the founder wealth objective, making attractive owner earnings highly volume-dependent and presently unsupported.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Energy advisers, suppliers, and reporting firms serving Polish SMEs form a concrete initial segment, and the scale of incumbent SME portfolios shows substantial underlying certificate volume. The economically addressable subset is not established: the proposed product matters only where buyer, site, or reporting-period reconciliation exceeds what suppliers already provide. The beachhead is therefore narrow enough to describe but not yet shown to be large or valuable enough to support the required outcome.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: TGE controls the registry and has added bulk handling and a marketplace, while large suppliers already bundle procurement and cancellation. Those actors own the customer relationship, registry access, and the ability to add similar reconciliation features. A startup dependent on one of them for essential actions has little bargaining power and no demonstrated route to dominate even the proposed niche.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A trusted reconciliation record could extend into reporting-platform integrations, multi-site allocation, exception handling, evidence for other energy attributes, and eventually additional geographies. Those adjacencies become credible only after winning a narrow evidence workflow, and Poland's lack of AIB Hub connection currently weakens the most obvious cross-border path. Expansion is plausible but not unlocked by a proven wedge.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Normalized invoice mappings, evidence templates, and accumulated exception histories could modestly improve product quality and switching costs. They are not inherently hard to reproduce, and the registry-capable partners supplying the data can internalize the workflow or sponsor alternatives. No exclusive access, embedded mandate, regulatory authorization, or proprietary dataset is demonstrated.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Buyer-specific reconciliation, expiry alerts, constrained claims wording, and a consolidated export may be more convenient than fragmented documents. The evidence does not show a decisive improvement in an outcome customers value enough to change behavior, and suppliers already provide renewable-origin coverage and cancellation. The offer is currently an incremental workflow enhancement rather than a compelling order-of-magnitude advantage.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Tighter EU rules on environmental claims and increasing demand for supportable evidence create a favorable reason to improve documentation. At the same time, TGE's 2026 bulk and marketplace capabilities and supplier bundling show that incumbents are modernizing the same workflow, while Poland's cross-border interoperability remains limited. Timing creates need but also accelerates feature absorption, yielding a mixed net effect.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Embedding through an adviser, supplier, or reporting platform is more plausible and founder-compatible than acquiring SMEs individually, and the family installer network can support a small referral test. No registry-capable partner has expressed signed interest or supplied commercial terms. The proposed channels are also substitutes with concentrated leverage, so repeatable acquisition, CAC, sales-cycle length, and access to end-customer demand remain unknown.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data and automation skills fit invoice reconciliation, exception detection, and evidence export, and a non-custodial pilot appears feasible part-time with limited capital. Material dependencies remain outside software execution: legal boundaries, registry eligibility and API access, partner contracting, permissible claim wording, and manual exception load. These are obtainable in principle but unresolved, and the essential partner cannot be replaced by AI or the founder's technical leverage.

highest_value_structural_change: Make a large buyer or supply-chain reporting platform—not the ordinary SME—the payer for a mandated exception-resolution and audit-evidence workflow across many suppliers; charge per verified evidence pack or portfolio licence only where existing supplier documents cannot satisfy buyer, site, and period matching, while a registry-capable counterparty retains all regulated actions and the startup controls the multi-supplier request, normalization, and exception record.
main_structural_strength: A capital-light, founder-compatible control point can join consumption records to registry-confirmed cancellation and produce narrower, more supportable evidence without taking certificate custody or trading risk.
primary_score_limiter: The entities required for registry access and distribution already bundle the core outcome, can absorb the reconciliation feature, and retain most of the bargaining power, leaving willingness to pay and durable margin unproven.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Axpo says renewable-origin coverage is provided to a Polish SME base of nearly 40000 customers without additional or hidden fees, directly contradicting a meaningful standalone subscription for ordinary SME guarantee-of-origin evidence.
